layers.note: A large shrub, sometimes a small tree, in thickets along washes and scattered on slopes.

moisture.note: Dry washes, arroyos and rocky slopes.

elevation_m.note: Below about 1,370 m in Arizona and 1,830 m in California, Texas and New Mexico (FEIS).

max_slope_deg.note: Wash banks, bajadas and rocky slopes.

shade_tolerance.note: Full sun; tolerates the light shade of desert trees.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about 2 to 20 °C; gone below −1 °C and above 24 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −16 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −22 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 24 to 36 °C; gone below 22 °C, where summers are too short, and above 39 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 4,000 to 11,000 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 3,000.

degree_days_5.note: About 2,600 to 9,000 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 1,800.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.05, gone by 0.02.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: it grows where winter rain falls alone (the Mojave and the low Colorado Desert) as well as where the July to September monsoon brings summer rain, as on the bajada (about half the year's); up to about 0.85 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.95.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m) from general knowledge of the species, the ranges and elevations in Kearney and Peebles (1942) and, where one exists, the FEIS species review. Catclaw acacia grows from southeastern California, southern Nevada and Utah through Arizona and New Mexico to western Texas and northern Mexico, across the Mojave, Sonoran and Chihuahuan deserts (FEIS). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
